subject.title: Feature request: fallback model chain for compaction and LCM summaryModel

question: Should OpenClaw add a core `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` config surface now, and should `plugins.entries.lossless-claw.config.summaryModel` fallback be owned by the Lossless plugin or by a generic context-engine SDK seam?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug fix: it adds provider/auth routing behavior and crosses the core compaction plus plugin-owned Lossless/context-engine boundary.

options.title: Approve Core Compaction Plus Plugin-Owned Lossless
options.body: Add an explicit core fallback chain for embedded compaction and keep Lossless `summaryModel` fallback in the Lossless plugin unless a missing SDK seam is proven.

options.title: Design A Unified Context-Engine Contract
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers choose one fallback API that covers embedded compaction, Lossless, and future context-engine summaries.

options.title: Keep Summarizer Fallbacks Outside Core
options.body: Decline a new core config key and ask operators to use provider plugins, compaction providers, or external routing for summarizer fallback behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve Core Compaction Plus Plugin-Owned Lossless
recommendation.body: Add an explicit core fallback chain for embedded compaction and keep Lossless `summaryModel` fallback in the Lossless plugin unless a missing SDK seam is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged context-engine compaction and runtime-context work is the closest history for deciding the core/plugin boundary of the Lossless half.
